overview.description: Spite and Malice (also known as Cat and Mouse) is a competitive patience game for two or more players, traditionally played with two or more standard decks of cards. It is the direct ancestor of the commercial game Skip-Bo. The objective is to be the first to move all cards from your personal 'pay-off pile' onto center 'build piles'. Kings are wild (or Jokers), and Aces start the piles.
overview.origin: United States (derived from Russian Bank / Crapette principles)

history.origins: Derived from Russian Bank (Crapette) principles but simpler. 'Spite' refers to blocking opponents.
timeline: 1900s: Included in Hoyle as 'Cat and Mouse'.
Present: Still played with standard cards by purists.
history.evolution: The use of Face Cards (J, Q, K) makes it slightly harder to read than numbered Skip-Bo cards.

setup.dealing: Shuffle both packs together. Deal 20 cards face down to each player's pay-off pile and 5 cards to each player's hand. Place the remainder face down as the stock. Turn the top card of each pay-off pile face up. The player with the higher pay-off card plays first (if equal, shuffle pay-off and turn a new top card).

rules.objective: Be the first to play all cards from your pay-off pile onto the center build stacks (ace through queen in sequence). Only the top card of your pay-off pile is playable at any time.
rules.gameplay: Shuffle both packs together. Each player has a face-down pay-off pile (20 cards) and a five-card hand; remainder is the stock. Turn order: player with higher pay-off top card plays first. On your turn, if you have fewer than five cards in hand, draw from stock to refill to five. You may then play cards to center stacks (ace to empty stack or next higher on existing, from hand, top of pay-off, or top of a side stack) or play one card from hand to one of your four side stacks, which ends your turn. Kings are wild. Max three center stacks; a completed stack (queen or king as queen) is shuffled into the stock by your opponent. You cannot play a pay-off card to a side stack or move cards between side stacks. If you play all five hand cards to the center without discarding, draw five more and continue.
keyRules: Center stacks: ace then 2 through queen; max three at a time.
Each player has up to four side stacks; playing to a side stack ends your turn.
Only the top card of pay-off and of each side stack is playable.

strategy.basic: Always check your Pay-off Pile card first. If it plays, play it. If not, check your hand/discards to see if you can make it play. Prioritize getting Pay-off cards out.
strategy.intermediate: Kings Usage: Save Kings for your Pay-off card. Don't waste a King to play a mundane card from your hand unless it unblocks your Pay-off.
strategy.advanced: Discard Stacking: Organize your 4 discard piles by rank (e.g., Pile 1 strict descending, Pile 2 trash). Don't bury useful cards. Watch opponent's Pay-off cardâ€”if they need a 7, and you have a 7, hold it.
tips: Keep an eye on the other player's top card.

list.name: Unlimited center stacks
list.description: Allow unlimited center stacks; completed stacks removed only when stock is depleted.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes only center stack limit; no engine constant overrides documented yet.

list.name: Compulsory play of aces
list.description: Aces must be played as soon as drawn or when on top of pay-off or side stack; no limit on number of center stacks.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds compulsory play rule; no engine overrides mapped for this variant yet.

list.name: Scoring
list.description: Winner scores 5 plus one per card left in opponent's pay-off pile; stalemate: score difference. Play to target (e.g. 50).
list.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring variant would need targetScore and scoringDirection overrides; not yet added.

difficulty.easy: Misses Pay-off moves; uses Kings randomly.
difficulty.hard: Expert 'Spite-Bot'; tracks opponent's Pay-off card; holds blockers; optimizes multi-step sequences to clear own pile.

phases.label: Play
phases.notes: Draw to five if needed, then play to center stacks or discard to a side stack (discard ends turn).

play_card.description: Play a card to a center stack (ace to empty or next higher on existing, from hand, top of pay-off pile, or top of a side stack) or play one card from hand to one of your four side stacks, which ends your turn. Cards played to center may be played in sequence; playing to a side stack is terminal.
play_card.constraints: Center: ace to empty stack or next rank on existing. Side stack: from hand only; max four side stacks per player; playing to side stack ends turn. Pay-off card cannot be played to a side stack.

draw.description: Draw cards from the stock at start of turn to refill hand to five cards.
draw.constraints: Only when hand has fewer than five cards; draw only from stock.

discard.description: Play one card from hand face-up onto one of your four side stacks. This ends your turn.
discard.constraints: From hand only; max four side stacks per player; cannot play pay-off card to side stack. Ends turn.

wildcards.restrictions: On center stack represents next higher than card it covers. May be discarded to side stack without committing to a rank.

edgeCases.text: Stock exhausted with no winner: game is a draw (or some play that player with fewer cards in pay-off pile wins).
Completed center stack (queen or king as queen): opponent shuffles it into the stock; you may continue playing.
If you play all five hand cards to the center without discarding, draw five more from stock and continue.

engine.handRankingSystem: First to empty pay-off pile wins; no hand ranking comparison.
engine.deckDescription: Two standard 52-card French decks shuffled together (104 cards). Each deck has four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) and thirteen ranks (Ace through King). Suits are irrelevant in play; Kings are wild. Optional jokers in some variants.
